words.technical: The computed trend has slipped to a hair below neutral because the horizons pull in opposite directions: the one-year component is still firmly positive and the quarter component is flat, but the half-year component is deeply negative and the 21-day reading sits close to zero. After a 1.5% weekly decline the price is a little below the middle of its one-year range, and daily volatility near 1.4% remains elevated for the metal. The stance is Flat; the flip to Wait lies about 5% lower, near $4,139, below the bottom of this week's computed range.
words.macro: Gold spent the week pinned under the rate outlook: markets priced about a 60% chance of a September Fed hike as trading opened on Tuesday, close to 70% by Friday morning, and about 90% after Friday's consumer-price report put core inflation at 0.3% for the month. With producer prices up 5.4% on the year, crude above $100 and the 10-year Treasury yield touching its highest level since October 2023, spot gold opened Friday at its lowest since early August and leaned on support near $4,300. The pressure named all week was the same pair — energy-driven inflation and the prospect of tighter policy — ahead of the 15–16 September Fed meeting.
words.long_term: The structural support — official-sector buying and heavy public-debt loads in the large economies — is unchanged; the test this autumn is a Fed that is weighing a hike rather than a cut.

eoy_scenarios.central: The September decision and the inflation data that follow leave real yields broadly where they are, and gold consolidates inside the central band while it waits for a new catalyst.
eoy_scenarios.upside: The Fed holds and oil-driven inflation erodes real returns elsewhere, reviving the debasement bid that carried the summer rally and lifting gold through the top of the band.
eoy_scenarios.downside: The Fed tightens and signals more to come, real yields and the dollar climb together, and the leveraged length still in the market unwinds through the bottom of the band.

words.technical: Silver's composite trend is modestly negative: the one-year component is strongly positive, but the quarter and half-year components are both clearly negative and the 21-day reading is flat after a 3.3% weekly fall. The price is in the lower third of its one-year range, and daily volatility near 2.6% is the highest of the metals, which keeps the computed ranges wide. The stance is Flat, and the flip to Wait sits roughly 9% below the market, near $58.85 — beneath the bottom of the one-week range.
words.macro: Silver fell harder than gold on the same forces. Spot traded near $65.70 on Tuesday as the oil spike kept Fed-hike bets alive, and the gold-to-silver ratio drifted up to about 66.7; the metal then opened Thursday at its strongest level of the week, near $67.90, before backing off ahead of the producer- and consumer-price reports. December futures opened Friday at $64.14, down 3.6% from a week earlier, as surging energy prices pushed analysts toward expecting a hike, and even a small Friday gain left futures lower on the week once hike odds climbed to about 90%.
words.long_term: The supply deficit tied to electrification and data-centre demand is intact, but silver's higher volatility means policy shocks hit it harder than gold in both directions.

eoy_scenarios.central: Industrial demand holds a floor under the price while tighter policy caps speculative buying, and silver chops inside the central band.
eoy_scenarios.upside: A Fed hold and a softer dollar bring momentum buyers back, and silver outpaces gold on the way up through the top of the band.
eoy_scenarios.downside: Rate-hike pressure and slowing industrial activity drain the remaining speculative length, and from the lower third of its range the metal slides through the bottom of the band.

words.technical: Crude carries the strongest trend on the board: the 21-day component is more than 1.6 standard deviations above normal after a 9.3% week, and the quarter and one-year components are positive too. The price sits in the upper quarter of its one-year range, and daily volatility above 3% is the widest of the seven instruments, which is why the one-week range spans roughly $92 to $109. The stance is Hold; the flip back to Flat is about 8.6% below the market, near $91.40, just under the bottom of that range.
words.macro: WTI gained more than 9% and crossed $100 for the first time since May as the US-Iran conflict spread through Gulf energy supply: new US strikes on Iranian tankers, attacks on Saudi energy infrastructure and explosions reported near Kharg Island opened the week, and Strait of Hormuz transits fell to seven ships on Thursday against a ten-day average of fifteen. The buffers are thin — the IEA put Saudi supply down 2.3 million barrels a day in August to about 6 million, the US strategic reserve is at its lowest since the early 1980s, and US crude and distillate stocks sit 5% and 13% below their five-year averages. Crude gave back more than 2% on Friday to settle near $100 as Iran and Gulf states were reported to be planning a meeting on a temporary Hormuz shipping arrangement.
words.long_term: Crude carries a war-risk premium tied to Gulf shipping that can widen or collapse on a single headline, so the long-run range stays unusually wide in both directions.

eoy_scenarios.central: Gulf shipping stays disrupted but not shut, supply from outside the region keeps growing into the gap, and crude holds inside the central band with the premium intact but no longer expanding.
eoy_scenarios.upside: The fighting reaches export infrastructure or closes the strait to commercial traffic, removing barrels the market cannot quickly replace and pushing crude above the band.
eoy_scenarios.downside: A ceasefire or a shipping arrangement strips out the war premium while high prices and higher rates weigh on demand, sending crude through the bottom of the band.

words.technical: Bitcoin's composite trend is barely positive and internally split: a strong quarter component is offset by negative half-year and one-year components, and the 21-day reading is mildly negative after a 3% weekly decline. The price sits almost exactly at the midpoint of its one-year range, with daily volatility near 2.1%. The stance is Flat; a close about 4% higher, near $80,500, would lift the composite far enough to flip it to Hold.
words.macro: Bitcoin tracked the rate outlook lower all week: it slid to about $78,500 on Tuesday as hike odds passed 60%, rising oil pressured risk assets and a hack hit a bitcoin layer-2 network; it traded near $77,000 on Thursday as the 10-year yield jumped to 4.96%, after spot bitcoin funds lost about $120 million on Wednesday in a second straight day of outflows; and it opened Friday near $76,500, its lowest in about two weeks and almost 6% below a week earlier. Smaller tokens fell harder, with the CoinDesk 20 index down about 3% over the day to Friday, roughly double bitcoin's decline. The main regulatory event ahead is a Senate procedural vote on the CLARITY Act market-structure bill, scheduled for 15 September.
words.long_term: Institutional ownership through listed funds and closer ties to traditional exchanges keep building the base, but the coin still trades as a high-volatility liquidity asset that answers to the rate outlook.

eoy_scenarios.central: Policy uncertainty keeps a lid on risk appetite without breaking it, and bitcoin trades sideways inside the central band.
eoy_scenarios.upside: The rate threat fades, fund inflows resume and regulatory clarity improves, carrying the coin through the top of the band.
eoy_scenarios.downside: A tightening cycle drains liquidity from speculative assets and fund outflows accelerate, pushing bitcoin through the bottom of the band.

words.technical: The index sits about nine-tenths of the way up its one-year range while its short-term momentum has turned down, with the 21-day reading roughly 0.45 standard deviations below normal after a 0.8% weekly loss. That combination — top of the range with fading momentum — is exactly what the script's Sell stance describes, even though the half-year and one-year components remain strongly positive and daily volatility is a low 0.7%. The flip back to Hold is about 1% lower, near 7,581: a dip that far would take the index out of the top band of its range and leave the underlying uptrend to set the stance.
words.macro: The S&P 500 lost about 0.8% over a four-session week as crude above $100 and accelerating producer prices, up 5.4% on the year, drove the 10-year Treasury yield to 4.98% overnight into Friday, its highest intraday level since October 2023. The index rebounded about 0.9% to 7,656 on Friday as oil pulled back, but the August consumer-price report showed prices up 3.4% on the year with core prices up 0.3% for the month, slightly above forecasts, and markets ended the week pricing a September Fed hike — the first since July 2023 — at close to 90%. Consumer sentiment also slid to 47.8 against 51.0 expected, with one-year inflation expectations rising to 4.6%.
words.long_term: Earnings growth led by the largest technology companies continues to underpin the index, but a price near the top of its one-year range leaves it sensitive to any repricing of rates.

eoy_scenarios.central: The Fed's path settles without a shock, earnings keep growing, and the index works sideways inside the central band after a strong year.
eoy_scenarios.upside: Inflation cools enough to take hikes off the table while profits keep beating, extending the rally through the top of the band.
eoy_scenarios.downside: The Fed tightens into an oil-price shock, margins and valuations compress together, and the index falls through the bottom of the band.

words.technical: The Nasdaq 100's composite trend stays positive on the strength of its half-year and one-year components, but the quarter component has faded to zero and the 21-day reading is about a third of a standard deviation below normal after a 0.6% weekly dip. The price is in the upper fifth of its one-year range, with daily volatility near 1%. The stance is Hold, but only just: the flip level is the current price itself, which means that as the lookback windows roll forward even an unchanged close would tip the stance to Flat.
words.macro: Technology shares took the same rate-and-oil shock as the wider market, and the Nasdaq Composite, the broader tech-heavy benchmark, finished the week about 0.7% lower despite a gain of nearly 1% on Friday. That rebound was led by hardware names, with Hewlett Packard Enterprise and Dell posting double-digit gains, while Nvidia was the only one of the seven largest technology stocks to close lower. Going into the week, Nasdaq 100 futures had been confined to a range of roughly 28,900 to 29,800, with a 10-year yield near 4.8%, oil above $90 and hike odds near 60% named as the headwinds.
words.long_term: AI-related spending by the largest platforms remains the index's engine, which concentrates both its gains and its exposure to a rates or demand scare in a handful of names.

eoy_scenarios.central: AI spending keeps delivering results while rates stay a worry rather than a shock, and the index grinds inside the central band on narrow leadership.
eoy_scenarios.upside: Leadership broadens beyond the largest names and policy turns benign, carrying the index through the top of the band.
eoy_scenarios.downside: Higher rates hit long-duration growth valuations and AI spending shows its first real slowdown, driving the index through the bottom of the band.

words.technical: The dollar index's composite trend is mildly negative: the 21-day component is about two-thirds of a standard deviation below normal and the quarter and half-year components are negative too, with only the one-year component positive. The price sits near the middle of its one-year range, and daily volatility under 0.3% keeps the one-week range narrow, roughly 98.3 to 99.9. The stance is Flat; the flip to Wait is only about 0.4% lower, near 98.67, so a modest slip in a week that contains a Fed decision would change it.
words.macro: The dollar index finished the week almost unchanged after pressure from both sides of the Atlantic: it gained 0.3% on Thursday as a stronger-than-expected US producer-price report lifted hike bets, on the same day the European Central Bank raised its rates by 25 basis points, taking the deposit rate to 2.50%. After Friday's consumer-price report the index touched 99.36 before slipping back to about 99.11 as a sharp drop in oil pulled long-dated yields lower, with markets pricing roughly an 88% chance of a Fed hike. With both central banks now tightening, it is the gap between them rather than either decision alone that the index is trading.
words.long_term: The dollar's long-run direction still hinges on how far US rates stay above those of the other major economies, and with the Fed and the ECB both tightening, the differential rather than either policy alone sets the course.

eoy_scenarios.central: The Fed and the ECB move in step, rate differentials stay roughly where they are, and the index holds inside the central band.
eoy_scenarios.upside: The Fed tightens further and faster than the other major central banks, widening the rate gap and lifting the dollar through the top of the band.
eoy_scenarios.downside: The US cycle stops after a single move while the ECB and others keep tightening, narrowing the gap and pushing the dollar through the bottom of the band.

week_summary: A week run by oil and inflation. Crude crossed $100 for the first time since May as the US-Iran conflict reached Gulf energy supply and Strait of Hormuz traffic dwindled; August producer prices accelerated to 5.4% on the year and consumer prices rose 3.4%, pushing the 10-year Treasury yield to its highest since October 2023 and the odds of a September Fed hike from about 60% to close to 90%, while the European Central Bank raised its own rates on Thursday. Gold, silver and bitcoin all fell on the tighter-policy outlook, the S&P 500 and Nasdaq 100 each lost under 1% despite a Friday rebound, oil gained more than 9%, and the dollar index finished flat ahead of the 15–16 September Fed meeting.
